submission.natural_language_explanation: A largely sense-insensitive lexical detector: it fires on the current token when that word form belongs to the vocabulary of vegetated land, farming and environmentalism (forest/Forest, woods, trees, grass, meadow, prairie, savanna, field, park, wilderness; farm/farmer(s), crops, soil, pasture, agriculture, livestock, hens; natural/naturally, environmental, sustainable, climate, green/Green, renewables, ecology, pollution, fracking, CO/carbon), and it fires even when the word is used in a non-ecological sense (natural numbers, a natural leader, environmental variables, a sustainable business model, server farm, field of mathematics, the CO as commanding officer, the actor Forest Whitaker). It stays inactive (below about a quarter of max) on words for water, weather and bare terrain (ocean, tide, lake, storm, snow, mountain, hills), on wild or pet animals (lion, dog, chicken), on urban or built-environment words (street, garage, bank), and on ordinary text with none of these word forms; the abstract nouns 'the nature of X' and 'programming environment' are weak exceptions.

rival_explanations: Sense-dependent ecology detector: it fires only when the word refers to the natural environment or land cultivation, so 'natural numbers', 'environmental variables', 'server farm' and 'the CO ordered' should be inactive (contradicted by measurement, but fits every top example).

Broad outdoor/natural-world detector: it fires on any word for the physical natural world, including water, weather, terrain and wild animals (ocean, storm, mountain, lion), not just vegetated land, farming and environmental-issue vocabulary.
